entities.evidence: יַהְוֶה names Yahweh, in whose presence Nimrod is described as a mighty hunter.
כְּנִמְרֹד means “like Nimrod.” The saying names the son of Cush introduced in Genesis 10:8.
The saying repeats לִפְנֵי יַהְוֶה, naming the same Yahweh as the opening clause.

name_review_base.evidence: יַהְוֶה names Yahweh, in whose presence Nimrod is described as a mighty hunter.
The saying names Nimrod and repeats the description of the son of Cush introduced in Genesis 10:8.
The saying repeats לִפְנֵי יַהְוֶה, naming the same Yahweh as the opening clause.

analysis.evidence: In הוּא הָיָה גִבֹּר צַיִד (“he was a mighty hunter”), הוּא is the subject of הָיָה (“was”). It refers to Nimrod, named again in כְּנִמְרֹד (“like Nimrod”).
analysis.morphology: Independent third-person masculine singular personal pronoun.

analysis.evidence: הָיָה links הוּא, referring to Nimrod, with the predicate גִבֹּר צַיִד, “a mighty hunter.” The saying in the second half of the verse repeats that description of Nimrod.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third-person masculine singular, agreeing with the subject הוּא.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: צַיִד specifies hunting as the activity in which Nimrod excels. The phrase גִבֹּר צַיִד means “a mighty hunter” and recurs in the saying “like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before YHWH.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular adjective in the construct state, used substantivally with צַיִד.

analysis.evidence: גִבֹּר צַיִד describes Nimrod as a mighty hunter. צַיִד names the activity in which he excels, and the proverb repeats the same description later in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase גִבֹּר צַיִד.

analysis.evidence: In גִבֹּר צַיִד לִפְנֵי יַהְוֶה, the phrase לִפְנֵי יַהְוֶה describes Nimrod as a mighty hunter in Yahweh’s sight. The saying in the second half of the verse repeats the phrase.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לִ־ combines with פְנֵי, the plural construct of פָּנִים, a common noun of both genders. Together they function as a preposition governing יַהְוֶה.
analysis.sense: before, in the presence of (a person, Yahweh)

analysis.morphology: Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In עַל כֵּן יֵאָמַר, “for this reason it is said,” כֵּן points back to Nimrod’s reputation as a mighty hunter before YHWH. עַל introduces that reputation as the reason for the saying.
כֵּן points back to the description of Nimrod as a mighty hunter before Yahweh. עַל כֵּן יֵאָמַר means “therefore it is said” and introduces the saying that repeats that description.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew demonstrative particle used adverbially with the separate preposition עַל. It has no attached prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: עַל כֵּן יֵאָמַר means “therefore it is said” and introduces the proverbial comparison beginning כְּנִמְרֹד, “like Nimrod.”
analysis.morphology: Niphal imperfect, third person masculine singular, used impersonally to express customary speech.

draft.change: Extend the existing Nimrod article’s summary and add Genesis 10:9 as evidence for his reputation as a hunter.
draft.definition: Nimrod, son of Cush, remembered as a mighty hunter before Yahweh.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:8 identifies Nimrod as Cush’s son. In Genesis 10:9, the saying names him as its standard of comparison with the words כְּנִמְרֹד, “like Nimrod.”

analysis.evidence: עַל כֵּן יֵאָמַר introduces the saying. After כְּנִמְרֹד, the saying repeats the opening description of a mighty hunter before Yahweh. Nimrod is the person to whom the comparison is made.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition כְּ means “like” and takes the personal name נִמְרֹד as its object.
analysis.sense: Nimrod, the mighty hunter cited in the saying.

analysis.evidence: In the saying כְּנִמְרֹד גִּבּוֹר צַיִד, צַיִד specifies hunting as the activity in which Nimrod excels. The saying repeats the description גִבֹּר צַיִד from the opening clause.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular adjective in the construct state, used substantivally with צַיִד.

analysis.evidence: In the saying about Nimrod, גִּבּוֹר צַיִד means “mighty hunter.” צַיִד names the activity in which he excels, repeating the description earlier in the verse.
